progress.intro: KOReader sends your position in a book to the server with its built-in progress sync — no plugins needed. Below is how to connect it and which settings decide when, and between which files, the position is carried over.

setup.title: Connecting
setup.device: Add the reader on the Devices screen — the panel will issue a device password. Each reader has its own password: you can revoke or change it without touching the others.
setup.server: In KOReader open the tools tab (wrench) → <progressSync/> → <customServer/> and enter the server address:
setup.login: Then <registerLogin/>: enter the username and the device password and tap <login/>.
setup.password: The password is the one the panel showed when you added the device. Lost it — issue a new one on the Devices screen.
setup.metadata: Turn on so the server knows book titles (details).

autoSync.title: When progress is sent
autoSync.default: Automatic sync in KOReader is off by default: progress reaches the server only when you choose . Without automatic sync, closing a book sends nothing.
autoSync.enabled: With <autoSync/> on, KOReader sends the position when you close a book, when the reader goes to sleep and when the network disconnects, and pulls the position from other devices when you open a book, wake the reader and connect to the network.
autoSync.pages: <syncEveryPages/> sends the position every N pages. It is available only with automatic sync on and does not turn Wi-Fi on by itself: it works only if the network is already connected.
autoSync.wifi: On readers where KOReader turns Wi-Fi on by itself, automatic sync requires settings (gear) → <network/> → <wifiAction/> set to <turnOn/>. Otherwise KOReader will not let you enable it and turns it off if it was on.
autoSync.logout: <logout/> in progress sync turns automatic sync on. If the reader used another server before and you logged out of it, automatic sync is most likely already on.

behavior.title: Sync behavior
behavior.intro: <syncBehavior/> sets what to do with a position that comes from the server.
behavior.time: “Newer” and “older” here are about time, not about the place in the book: KOReader compares when the position was saved on the other device with its own last page turn. If you later went back to the start of a chapter on your phone, the phone's position is newer even though it is closer to the beginning.
behavior.newer: <syncNewer/> — what to do with a newer position. By default KOReader asks.
behavior.older: <syncOlder/> — what to do with an older one. By default nothing: it is not applied.

metadata.title: Document metadata
metadata.text: With the progress KOReader sends only a hash of the file, not the title. With on, it adds the title, authors and file name. Without it the book shows up in the panel as unknown until the title comes from reading statistics. The option is available in KOReader 2026.07 and later.

matching.title: Document matching
matching.intro: <matchingMethod/> decides which files on different readers count as the same book.
matching.binary: <matchingBinary/> — the default. The position is shared only between byte-for-byte identical files.
matching.filename: <matchingFilename/> — the position is shared between files with the same name. Titles from reading statistics are not matched to such books: statistics identifies books by the file contents.
matching.same: Use the same method on all readers: with different methods the position is not carried over between them.

formats.title: Different files of the same book
formats.text: For the server a book is a specific file. FB2 and EPUB of the same book, as well as a file changed after copying (for example, by editing metadata in a library manager), are different books, and the position is not carried over between them. To read on several devices, copy the same file to all of them.

statistics.intro: KOReader syncs reading statistics and the vocabulary through cloud storage, and the server connects to it as WebDAV. No plugins needed.

what.title: What reaches the server
what.text: From KOReader statistics — reading time and pages for each book. The server keeps one snapshot per user: on every sync a reader merges its statistics with it, so the snapshot covers all your readers.
what.vocabulary: The vocabulary is synced and stored on the server too, but the panel does not show it yet.

setup.title: Setup
setup.version: These steps are for KOReader 2026.07 and later (why).
setup.credentials: Username — {{username}}, password — the device password, the same as for progress sync. Leave the start folder empty.

cloudStorage.title: Which cloud storage to use
cloudStorage.text: KOReader 2026.07 has two storages in the menu: <cloudStorage/> and <cloudStoragePlus/>. Statistics and the vocabulary sync only through <cloudStoragePlus/>, and the old storage has its own server list: a server added there does not appear in <cloudSync/>. Newer versions removed the old storage and kept a single <cloudStorage/> item.
cloudStorage.old: Versions before 2026.07 have no <cloudStoragePlus/> plugin and statistics syncs through the old storage. That path has not been tested with this server.

sync.title: When it syncs
sync.text: There is no timer: sync runs manually or by a gesture assigned to it. Statistics — <readingStatistics/> → <syncNow/>. Vocabulary — the “⇅” button at the bottom of the vocabulary window or <syncNow/> in its <cloudSync/>.
sync.disabled: <syncNow/> in statistics stays disabled until a server is selected in <cloudSync/>.

vocabulary.title: Vocabulary
vocabulary.text: Open <vocabularyBuilder/>, tap the menu in the window title → <cloudSync/> and select the same server and folder as for statistics.

upload.title: Uploading a file from the panel
upload.text: You can also upload the statistics file manually — on the Devices screen, in the Reading statistics card. It is statistics.sqlite3 from the KOReader settings folder. The file is merged with the statistics on the server, nothing is deleted; readers get the data on their next sync.

folders.title: Folders on the server
folders.text: KOReader cannot create a folder on the server: statistics and vocabulary files live in the root. So leave the start folder empty and pick the root in <cloudSync/> — long-press <chooseFolder/>.

numbers.title: How the numbers are counted
numbers.days: Days and hours follow the time zone of the browser the panel is open in. On the reader, KOReader uses the reader's own time zone, so with a different zone reading around midnight may land on the neighbouring day.
numbers.pages: Pages are converted to the book's current layout, as in KOReader: if the font or page size changed, old records are mapped to today's pages. A page counts once per day, and pages for a week, month or year are the sum of daily pages. KOReader's weekly and monthly summaries count a page once per week or month, so you may see more pages here.
numbers.sessions: A session is reading one book with pauses no longer than 10 minutes. KOReader does not store sessions; the server derives them. Sessions have no device: statistics on the server merge all your readers.
numbers.noData: Days after the last statistics sync are hatched: the server has no data for them yet, which is not the same as no reading. While the period has such days, the comparison with the previous period is replaced by how many days have data.
numbers.book: For a book: “p. N of M” is the percentage of the last progress sync converted to pages using the book's page count from statistics, so it is approximate if readers lay out the book differently. “≈ left” is the remaining pages times the average time per page, as in KOReader: a single page counts for at most 2 minutes (KOReader's default; if the reader uses a different limit, the estimates will differ). “+N % today” is how much the percentage grew since the last sync before the start of the day.

troubleshooting.intro: Symptom, cause and what to do. KOReader does not translate the messages that come from the server.

loginFailed.title: KOReader says “Unauthorized” on login
loginFailed.cause: This is the server's response: wrong username or device password, or the device has been revoked. It needs the device password, not the panel one.
loginFailed.fix: Check the username. If the password is lost or the device is revoked, issue a new password or add a device on the Devices screen and log in again (connecting).
loginFailed.note: KOReader shows “Cannot login: invalid username and password” by itself, without contacting the server: a field was left empty.

tooManyAttempts.title: “Too many failed attempts. Try again in N minutes.” on login
tooManyAttempts.cause: After several failed logins the server temporarily blocks logins from this address.
tooManyAttempts.fix: Wait for the stated time, check the username and device password and log in again.

syncRejected.title: Login worked, but later — “Something went wrong when syncing progress…”
syncRejected.cause: The device has been revoked or issued a new password. KOReader keeps the key from the login and does not log in again, and it does not queue a rejected request: a manual push or pull shows this message, automatic sync silently sends nothing.
syncRejected.fix: Issue a new password on the Devices screen, then in KOReader → → with the new password. If the device was not revoked and the password did not change — the server is unreachable.

noProgress.title: Progress does not show up in the panel
noProgress.cause: Automatic sync is off in KOReader (the default) or there was no network at the moment of sending.
noProgress.fix: Turn on or send progress manually: . When progress is sent.

unknownBook.title: The book shows up as “Unknown book”
unknownBook.cause: The server knows the book only by the file hash: <sendMetadata/> is off in KOReader, the statistics on the server do not have this book, and its file is not in the server library.
unknownBook.fix: Turn on (KOReader 2026.07 and later) — the title arrives with the next sync. Or set up statistics sync: the title and authors are taken from it. Or put the book file into a server library folder (added by the administrator) — the title is taken from the file after a scan. Document metadata.

differentBooks.title: Another reader does not pick up the position
differentBooks.cause: For the server these are different books: the files differ (FB2 and EPUB, metadata edited after copying) or the readers use a different <matchingMethod/>. The panel shows such files as separate books. If it is one book, the position arrived but KOReader did not apply it — that is set in <behavior>sync behavior</behavior>.
differentBooks.fix: Copy the same file to all readers and use the same matching method on all of them. Details: <formats>different files of the same book</formats>, <matching>document matching</matching>.

unknownServerError.title: “Unknown server error” on login or “Something went wrong…” on sync, though the device was not revoked
unknownServerError.cause: The reader could not reach the server, or a proxy in front of the server answered instead of it: with a gateway error or its own login page.
unknownServerError.fix: Open the address from in a browser on another device in the same network as the reader: this panel should open. If the device was revoked or issued a new password, “Something went wrong…” has another cause.

statsSyncDisabled.title: <syncNow/> in statistics is disabled
statsSyncDisabled.cause: No server is selected in the statistics <cloudSync/>.
statsSyncDisabled.fix: → → : select the WebDAV server and the root folder. Setup.

statsWrongStorage.title: The WebDAV server is added but missing from <cloudSync/>
statsWrongStorage.cause: The server was added to the old <cloudStorage/>, while in KOReader 2026.07 statistics syncs only through <cloudStoragePlus/>.
statsWrongStorage.fix: Add the server to . Which storage to use.

statsNoTitles.title: Statistics arrived, but books in the panel have no titles
statsNoTitles.cause: The reader uses <matchingFilename/> in <matchingMethod/>: statistics identifies books by the file contents, while progress then comes by file name, and the books do not match.
statsNoTitles.fix: Turn on — titles will come with the progress — or choose . Or put these book files into the server library: the file name hash finds them there. Document matching.

conversionFailed.title: The “To EPUB” button reports an error
conversionFailed.cause: The FB2 file is damaged, too large (over 128 MiB unpacked), or the conversion did not finish within 5 minutes. Behind a reverse proxy the error also appears when the proxy stops waiting while the work goes on.
conversionFailed.fix: If the file is damaged, replace it in the library. If time ran out or the connection dropped, press “To EPUB” again: the result may already be saved.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.description: Reading time and pages from KOReader statistics. Days and hours follow this browser's time zone.
stats.noPrevious: no reading in the previous period
stats.noDataHint: There is no data for the hatched days yet: statistics will update once you sync them on the reader.

empty.title: No statistics yet
empty.text: Reading time, pages, sessions and the calendar come from KOReader statistics via cloud sync (WebDAV). Set it up on the reader or upload the statistics file below.
